scenario: AITA for telling my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together? | My girlfriend expects me to build a future for us. A little back story: She's a student right now and works part time but barely makes enough to pay her rent/school fees. I'm 24 and work a minimum wage + commission job, I have barely any money saved so she doesn't understand why I spend so much money/time with family We've been dating 3 years with no problems except for this, we love each other and live independent lives but she worries that I'm too focused on helping my family and making them happy instead of building a future for us. She's working as much as she can to pay her bills but because shes a student and also doing her required interning she can't work much more. She doesnt ever ask me for money to help her right now because she wants me to save up. She doesn't have a family like mine so she doesn't understand, my family is close and I really want to take care of them. She says that I'm supposed to be worrying about my own future right now. She says that she doesn't understand because my mom recently received about ~100k for a settlement and bought a house and a new car and I shouldn't be worrying about helping when they seem fine. She is angry that I dont take my life seriously, I've been trying to get my real estate license for a few months now but cant find the time to study because of how demanding my family is, they get really angry/sad when I'm not around for family events and I understand why, we're a close family. I get where shes coming from but I cant drop my family. I told her all of this and she got angry saying that shes not asking me to abandon my family, she just wants to make sure we have a solid foundation before we worry about helping my family. And I cant build a future if I'm always with them. She expects me to start saving up money for a downpayment on a house while she finishes and gets her degree and can start helping as well but I keep telling her my family needs me first. We had a particularly heated fight, the worst we've ever had last night and she said she feels like I'll never care enough about my future and I'm supposed to be building one for myself and her and she can't be with someone like that. She said if I really feel like helping my family comes before my own future than that is my choice but she's going to have no choice but to worry about herself from now on and plan a future where shes her only priority because I make it sound like I don't want to be part of it. Shes stopped mentioning anything about it and is now talking about saving up for a one bedroom apartment and a car for herself (she lives in a basement). She seems so sad but I cant help but feel like shes wrong for even asking me to not help my family. I dont know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family will always come first. AITA for telling her my family and their needs have to come before her and our future together?

When partners feel like they’re not a priority, resentment builds. 3. **Financial and Emotional Strain on Her** - She’s in a **precarious financial situation** (student debt, part-time work, no safety net), and you’re not helping her stabilize. While she’s not asking for money, she’s **right to expect shared effort** toward a future. If you’re not saving for a down payment, getting a better job, or even discussing long-term goals, she has every right to feel abandoned. - Her recent shift—planning for a future **without you**—is a **clear sign of emotional withdrawal**. This is not healthy for either of you. 4. **Cultural Context Doesn’t Excuse Neglect** - While family is central in many African cultures, **that doesn’t mean you should neglect your partner’s needs entirely**. The best relationships involve **both partners contributing to each other’s growth**. - If your family is truly struggling (despite the settlement), there are **ways to help without derailing your own life**. For example: - Setting **clear financial boundaries** (e.g., "I’ll contribute X amount to family needs, but my primary focus is saving for us"). - Involving her in family decisions (e.g., "Let’s discuss how we can support my family while also planning for our future"). - Finding **efficient ways to help** (e.g., one-time financial support instead of constant emotional/physical presence). 5. **Her Reaction Is Valid** - She’s not being unreasonable. **No one should have to choose between their partner’s future and their own happiness.** If you truly love her, you should want to **build a life with her**, not just tolerate her presence while prioritizing others. - Her sadness isn’t just about money—it’s about **feeling like she’s not enough**. When a partner consistently puts others first, it creates a **power imbalance** in the relationship. --- ### **Why It’s Not Entirely Your Fault (But Still Wrong)** - **You’re caught in a cultural expectation** that may not align with modern relationship dynamics. Many African families value extended family heavily, but **romantic partnerships are also about mutual care and shared goals**. - **You’ve been trying to study for your real estate license**, which is a step in the right direction. But **action without balance is still insufficient**. - **She’s not asking you to abandon your family—she’s asking for fairness**. There’s a difference between helping family and **neglecting your own life and hers**. --- ### **What You Should Do Now** 1. **Acknowledge Her Feelings (Without Defensiveness)** - Instead of saying *"Family always comes first,"* try: > *"I love my family, and I want to support them, but I also want to build a future with you. I realize I haven’t been doing enough to balance both, and I’m sorry for making you feel like a second priority. Let’s figure out how we can both contribute to our future while still honoring my family."* 2. **Set Clear Boundaries with Your Family** - **Negotiate time and financial contributions** so you’re not always available. For example: - *"I’ll be there for major family events, but I need to prioritize my own goals and ours."* - *"I’ll help with family needs, but I also need to save for our future."* 3. **Start Taking Concrete Steps for Your Future** - **Stop making excuses** about not having time to study for your license. If you’re serious about a better future, **block out time**—even if it means saying no to some family demands. - **Save aggressively** (even small amounts) for a down payment. If you can’t yet, **start a side hustle** or look for a better-paying job. 4. **Reaffirm Your Commitment to Her** - She’s been patient for three years, but **silence and excuses are not love**. Show her through **actions** (not just words) that she matters. - If she’s planning for a future **without you**, that’s a **serious red flag**. You need to **prove you’re willing to fight for her**—not just tolerate her. 5. **Consider Couples Therapy (If Needed)** - If you can’t communicate this without fighting, a mediator might help you **find a middle ground** that respects both your family and her needs. --- ### **Final Verdict: You Were Wrong to Frame It This Way** Saying *"family always comes first"* is **not a healthy foundation for a relationship**. Love should mean **balancing responsibilities**—not making one person feel like an afterthought. **You can honor your family without abandoning your partner.** The question is: **Are you willing to make the effort?** If you’re not, then **she’s right to walk away**—because a relationship where one person is always the priority is not a partnership, and it won’t last.
